In mathematics, a '''nullform''' of a [[vector space]] [[Group action (mathematics)|acted]] on [[linear map|linearly]] by a [[group (mathematics)|group]] is a vector on which all [[Invariant theory|invariants]] of the group vanish. Nullforms were introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Hilbert|year=1893|authorlink=David Hilbert}}.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dieudonné |first=Jean A |authorlink=Jean Dieudonné |last2=Carrell |first2=James B |authorlink2=James B. Carrell |date=February 1970 |title=Invariant theory, old and new |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |language=en |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=1–80 |doi=10.1016/0001-8708(70)90015-0|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hilbert |first=David |date=September 1893 |title=Ueber die vollen Invariantensysteme |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01444162 |journal=Mathematische Annalen |language=de |volume=42 |issue=3 |pages=313–373 |doi=10.1007/BF01444162 |issn=0025-5831|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
